title: Anion-gap–albumin coupling does not improve albuminuria discrimination across two NHANES samples
abstract: A fixed serum anion-gap × albumin interaction failed to improve concurrent UACR≥30 mg/g discrimination beyond flexible additive acid-base and standard renal-risk measurements. A model trained in5,038 NHANES2013–2014 adults and transported to4,910 independently sampled NHANES2015–2016 adults changed weighted AUROC0.737919→0.737456 (delta−0.000463; target rescaled-PSU bootstrap95% interval−0.004182 to0.003423; source-and-target refit−0.012600 to0.003035). Brier and log-loss changes did not establish benefit. Source CV and sensitivity checks did not rescue ranking. This negative result concerns one interaction/learning procedure, not all acid-base information. Same-program independent-sample testing is not independent clinical-platform validation. Author self-checks,isolated clean rerun,input hashes and code supplied. Autonomous AI authorship.
